method: Linux cgroup-v2 512 MiB memory.max, swap.max=0; mixed FakeLLM workload; CPU affinity logical CPUs 0,1; sequential ABBA
source_environment: WSL Debian; native Linux git clones and /tmp ext4 scratch, same Python and fixed benchmark script across old/new
runner_reproduction_note: Measured wrapper defaulted locally to the unprivileged user recorded per resource sidecar; attachment requires explicit --user and otherwise uses the same cap and counter mechanism.
semantics: Four sequential ABBA runs, synthetic FakeLLM and in-memory platform; no real traffic.
Each run: 12 inbound observations, 24 timed chat model calls, 12 timed successful sends plus one warmup send.
Each run: 12 reflection arrivals and 12 Work renew arrivals; seven actual reflection receipts, identical original sources in all runs.
Pooled model and receipt distributions use all 24 per-input raw samples for each product; not means of per-run percentiles.
Handler is handle entry to return; scheduled arrival to confirmed receipt is the stronger completion measure.
Resource sidecars cover whole child lifetime, not only timed workload. memory.peak is cgroup charged memory, not process RSS.
Sampled callback dispatch delay is a 20Hz sampled measurement, not continuous maximum event-loop stall.
512 MiB cap was enforced but not approached: all memory.max/oom/oom_kill counters are zero; this is not proof under near-cap memory pressure.
Prior full ABBA failed before timing because native Linux Git could not resolve Windows worktree pointers; retained separately and not mixed into valid latency samples.

benchmark.head: c2ce7da66ab54efe192993b9615df48266a62137
benchmark.dataset: synthetic logical fixture; setup and post-run verification are untimed
benchmark.model_transport: fixed FakeLLMProvider and in-memory platform; no real requests
benchmark.completion_semantics: Original event ID and unique body must occur in an actual Fake model request linked to a successful Social receipt for its current source; history observations may share a reply. Work inputs must be consumed and original producers joined. This is not one reply per arrival.
benchmark.handler_semantics: processor.handle entry to return; merged inputs can return before their producer finishes
benchmark.arrival_to_exit_semantics: original scheduled arrival to processor.handle return, including late coroutine dispatch
benchmark.receipt_completion_semantics: perf_counter observed when original Social._dispatch_claimed returns a successful receipt after its actual ledger/receipt commit; matched to a model request that observed the input before that completion. Latency starts at original scheduled arrival, never a DB created_at.
benchmark.elapsed_semantics: scheduled load start through input drain and shared diagnostic writer drain; post-run verification excluded
benchmark.callback_probe_semantics: 20 Hz sleeping thread posts callbacks; perf_counter measures post to event-loop dispatch. Sampled delays do not measure continuous maximum stall or time when the observer cannot acquire the GIL.
benchmark.acknowledged_write_semantics: all Session root transactions; starts after BEGIN IMMEDIATE or first successful DML; a lower bound on actual SQLite writer hold time, excluding the first SQL duration
benchmark.phase_semantics: entry_wait includes checkout/BEGIN; scope_and_exit starts after BEGIN and includes physical commit/cleanup; explicit immediate scopes only, baseline mixed sessions are excluded from these two distributions

resources.semantics: memory.max is a real memory-cgroup limit, not RLIMIT_AS or an RSS promise. memory.peak includes charged memory/cache/kernel pages for the leaf and descendants. io.stat is kernel-accounted device I/O; empty remains empty, not fabricated activity. All sidecar resource counters cover the whole child lifetime. Original benchmark JSON remains the timed workload evidence.

benchmark.arrival_to_exit_semantics: original scheduled arrival to processor.handle return, including late coroutine dispatch
benchmark.receipt_completion_semantics: perf_counter observed when original Social._dispatch_claimed returns a successful receipt after its actual ledger/receipt commit; matched to a model request that observed the input before that completion. Latency starts at original scheduled arrival, never a DB created_at.
benchmark.elapsed_semantics: scheduled load start through input drain and shared diagnostic writer drain; post-run verification excluded
benchmark.callback_probe_semantics: 20 Hz sleeping thread posts callbacks; perf_counter measures post to event-loop dispatch. Sampled delays do not measure continuous maximum stall or time when the observer cannot acquire the GIL.
benchmark.acknowledged_write_semantics: all Session root transactions; starts after BEGIN IMMEDIATE or first successful DML; a lower bound on actual SQLite writer hold time, excluding the first SQL duration
benchmark.phase_semantics: entry_wait includes checkout/BEGIN; scope_and_exit starts after BEGIN and includes physical commit/cleanup; explicit immediate scopes only, baseline mixed sessions are excluded from these two distributions

resources.semantics: memory.max is a real memory-cgroup limit, not RLIMIT_AS or an RSS promise. memory.peak includes charged memory/cache/kernel pages for the leaf and descendants. io.stat is kernel-accounted device I/O; empty remains empty, not fabricated activity. All sidecar resource counters cover the whole child lifetime. Original benchmark JSON remains the timed workload evidence.
